predecessors.name: Liang dynasty
predecessors.text: the Chen's core in 557-559: the south of China from Jiankang to Lingnan, without Wang Lin's Hunan and eastern Hubei

successors.name: Sui dynasty
successors.text: the whole Chen realm, taken when Jiankang fell in 589

ledger.x: 557: Chen Baxian founds the Chen at Jiankang.
560: the Chen take Hunan and half of Xiao Zhuang's land.
561: the Western Liang cedes the other half.
573: the Chen take the land between the Yangtze and the Huai.
580: the Zhou finish the northern campaign.
580: the Chen lose the north bank of the Yangtze.
587: two Western Liang officials surrender to the Chen.
589: the Chen falls and China is reunited.

wars.name: Chen-Wang Lin war
wars.outcome: Chen victory: Hou Tian beat Wang Lin in spring 560; Wang and Xiao Zhuang fled to the Northern Qi; the Chen took about half of Xiao Zhuang's territory and the Western Liang ceded the other half in spring 561.

wars.name: Chen northern expedition of 573
wars.outcome: Chen victory: Wu Mingche gained most of the land between the Yangtze and the Huai; Shouyang was taken and the Qi commander Wang Lin killed.

wars.name: Chen-Zhou war over Huainan
wars.outcome: Zhou victory: the Chen siege of Pengcheng failed in spring 578 (Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche) and by new year 580 the Zhou held nearly all the land north of the Yangtze.

wars.name: Ouyang He's rebellion
wars.outcome: Crushed: Ouyang He was beheaded in 570.

wars.name: Sui conquest of the Chen
wars.outcome: Sui victory: Jiankang fell in spring 589 (infobox 10 February) and Chen Shubao was captured.

certainty.note: The northern frontier on the Yangtze-Huai strip moved by campaign in 573 and 579-580; no treaty or survey fixes the frontiers with the Qi, the Zhou or the Western Liang, and the Lingnan and Jiaozhou edges are approximate.
